Definition: from G3844 and G1209; to accept near, i.e. admit or (by implication) delight in:--receive.
BiblicalUsage: Paradechomai is to receive, to accept, to admit. The seed sown on good ground hears the word and receives it and brings forth fruit, Paul is told in a vision to make haste out of Jerusalem for they will not receive thy testimony concerning Me, and the Lord's chastening is received by the son whom He loves.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe receiving is the hinge of the gospel. The good ground receives the word, Jerusalem refuses the testimony, and the son receives the chastening — and the fruit tells which is which.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
